sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Rudiobus is a Continental Celtic god. He is an obscure Gaulish god known from a single item, a statue of a horse. That piece may show the god in horse form, or it may be an offering made to him. People link him with the Romano-Celtic god Mars. That god is also called Mullo, a name that may mean mule.

okr.objective: Present Rudiobus as an obscure Gaulish god tied to the horse statue and Mars.
key_results: He is known from a single horse statue.
The statue may show the god or serve as an offering.
He is joined to the Romano-Celtic god Mars.
Mars appears under the name Mullo, possibly mule.
